arxiv-1612-04251.title: TF.Learn: TensorFlow’s High-level Module for Distributed Machine Learning
arxiv-1612-04251.creator: Yuan Tang terry.tang@uptake.com
arxiv-1612-04251.description: Abstract TF.Learn is a high-level Python module for distributed machine learning inside TensorFlow ( Abadi et al. 2015 ) . It provides an easy-to-use Scikit-learn ( Pedregosa et al. 2011 ) style interface to simplify the process of creating, configuring, training, evaluating, and experimenting a machine learning model. TF.

arxiv-2206-13334.title: Butler’s method applied to 𝑍 p [ C p × C p ] \Z_{p}[C_{p}\times C_{p}] -permutation modules
arxiv-2206-13334.creator: John W. MacQuarrie, Marlon Stefano
arxiv-2206-13334.description: Abstract Let G G be a finite p p -group with normal subgroup N N of order p p . The first author and Zalesskii have previously given a characterization of permutation modules for 𝑍 p G \Z_{p}G in terms of modules for G / N G/N , but the necessity of their conditions was not known.

arxiv-2210-17137.title: Split-harmonic maps and the interpolation problem for timelike minimal surfaces
arxiv-2210-17137.creator: Sreedev Manikoth
arxiv-2210-17137.description: Abstract The singular Björling problem and its solution for timelike minimal surfaces is a well-known result in minimal surface theory. In this article, we give a different proof of this theorem using split-harmonic maps. This is motivated by a similar solution of the singular Björling problem for maximal surfaces using harmonic maps.

arxiv-2302-04094.title: Learning Graph-Enhanced Commander-Executor for Multi-Agent Navigation Conference: Proc. of the 22nd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2023); May 29 – June 2, 2023; London, United Kingdom 442
arxiv-2302-04094.creator: Xinyi Yang 1 , Shiyu Huang 2 , Yiwen Sun 3 , Yuxiang Yang 1 , Chao Yu 1,4 , Wei-Wei Tu 2 , Huazhong Yang 1† , Yu Wang 1†
arxiv-2302-04094.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xinyi Yang 1 , Shiyu Huang 2 , Yiwen Sun 3 , Yuxiang Yang 1 , Chao Yu 1,4 , Wei-Wei Tu 2 , Huazhong Yang 1† , Yu Wang 1†. This paper investigates the multi-agent navigation problem, which requires multiple agents to reach the target goals in a limited time. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has shown promising results for solving this issue.

arxiv-2306-00582.title: Anomaly Detection with Variance Stabilized Density Estimation
arxiv-2306-00582.creator: Amit Rozner, Barak Battash, Henry Li, Lior Wolf, Ofir Lindenbaum
arxiv-2306-00582.description: Abstract We propose a modified density estimation problem that is highly effective for detecting anomalies in tabular data. Our approach assumes that the density function is relatively stable (with lower variance) around normal samples. We have verified this hypothesis empirically using a wide range of real-world data.

arxiv-2403-00027.title: A Quick Framework for Evaluating Worst Robustness of Complex Networks
arxiv-2403-00027.creator: Wenjun Jiang, Peiyan Li, Tianlong Fan, Ting Li, Chuan-fu Zhang, Tao Zhang, Zong-fu Luo
arxiv-2403-00027.description: Abstract Robustness is pivotal for comprehending, designing, optimizing, and rehabilitating networks, with simulation attacks being the prevailing evaluation method. Simulation attacks are often time-consuming or even impractical, however, a more crucial yet persistently overlooked drawback is that any attack strategy merely provides a potential paradigm of disintegration.

arxiv-2410-09648.title: Advancing Experimental Platforms for UAV Communications: Insights from AERPAW’S Digital Twin
arxiv-2410-09648.creator: Joshua Moore, Aly S. Abdalla, Charles Ueltschey, Anıl Gürses , Özgür Özdemir, Mihail L. Sichitiu, Ismail Güvenç, and Vuk Marojevic
arxiv-2410-09648.description: Abstract The rapid evolution of 5G and beyond has advanced space-air-terrestrial networks, with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offering enhanced coverage, flexible configurations, and cost efficiency. However, deploying UAV-based systems presents challenges including varying propagation conditions and hardware limitations. While simulators and theoretical models have been developed, real-world experimentation is critically important to validate the research.

arxiv-2502-18835.title: Music Therapy based Stress Prediction using Homological Feature Analysis on EEG Signals
arxiv-2502-18835.creator: Srikireddy Dhanunjay Reddy, Tharun Kumar Reddy Bollu
arxiv-2502-18835.description: Abstract Stress became a common factor in the busy daily routines of all academic and corporate working environments. Everyone checks for efficient stress-buster alternatives to calm down from work pressure. Instead of investing time in unnecessary efforts, this work shows the stress relief scenario of subjects by listening to ”Raag Darbari” music notes as a simple add-on to their schedule.

arxiv-2510-11064.title: Detecting Gender Stereotypes in Scratch Programming Tutorials Conference: 25th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research; November 11–16, 2025; Koli, Finland 25th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research (Koli Calling ’25), November 11–16, 202
arxiv-2510-11064.creator: Isabella Graßl, Benedikt Fein, Gordon Fraser
arxiv-2510-11064.description: Abstract . Gender stereotypes in introductory programming courses often go unnoticed, yet they can negatively influence young learners’ interest and learning, particularly underrepresented groups such as girls. Popular tutorials on block-based programming with Scratch may unintentionally reinforce biases through character choices, narrative framing, or activity types. Educators currently lack support in identifying and addressing such bias.

The Arabidopsis root, with its simple structure and indeterminate growth, is an ideal model for investigating the spatiotemporal transcriptional signatures underlying developmental...

pmc-12462369.title: Firearm injury and young children: a critical review
pmc-12462369.creator: Alison L Miller, Wadad Itani, Hurley Riley, Ezekiel Medina, Odalys Arbelaez, Julia Plawker, Andrew Hashikawa, Daniel Lee, Justin Heinze, Cynthia Ewell-Foster, Rebeccah Sokol, Hsing-Fang Hsieh
pmc-12462369.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Firearms are the leading cause of death in children in the United States. Rates of firearm injury and death are rising among young children, ages 0–5 years, yet data-driven prevention strategies are lacking. The goal of this critical review was to provide a developmentally-informed overview of the patterns and prevalence, contexts, and impacts for all-cause firearm injury among children ages 0–5 years. We review findings from interdisciplinary, peer-reviewed studies to inform considerations for prevention strategies.

pmc-12690744.title: PDNO-12 PEDIATRIC SUPRATENTORIAL EPENDYMOMA; INSIGHT FROM A TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL
pmc-12690744.creator: Farrah Bashir, Soha Zahid, Bilal Mazhar Qureshi, Ather Enam, Khurram Minhas, Naureen Mushtaq
pmc-12690744.description: BackgroundPediatric ependymoma is a distinct entity with a variable prognosis according to the age and location of the tumor. Supratentorial ependymoma accounts for almost one-third of the total pediatric ependymoma. We aim to present our experience of supratentorial ependymomas over a 10-year period at a single tertiary care hospital in Pakistan.

pmc-12926810.title: Documentation of Stigmatizing Language in Electronic Health Records and Birth Outcomes
pmc-12926810.creator: Jihye Kim Scroggins, Ismael Ibrahim Hulchafo, Sarah Harkins, Hans Moen, Michele Tadiello, Kenrick Cato, Anahita Davoudi, Dena Goffman, Janice James Aubey, Coretta Green, Maxim Topaz, Veronica Barcelona
pmc-12926810.description: Introduction:Stigmatizing language represents biases. Understanding its impact is crucial to improve perinatal health. We aimed to examine the association between stigmatizing language in electronic health records (EHR) and birth outcomes.Methods:We analyzed EHR data of patients admitted for childbirth (n = 18,897) between 2017 and 2019 using natural language processing at two hospitals in the United States.

pmc-12957898.title: Advancing Raman Calibration: Automated Data Generation, Monitoring, and Control in Multi‐Parallel Perfusion Mini Bioreactors
pmc-12957898.creator: Rafael Machleid, Maximilian Goertz, Christian Grimm, Johan Trygg, Sven Mathias, Izabella Surowiec
pmc-12957898.description: The biopharmaceutical industry is transitioning towards more efficient and cost‐effective production methods, driven by the need for more affordable treatments. Process intensifications techniques, such as perfusion are the means by which the biopharmaceutical industry is trying to lower costs, enhance productivity and product quality, and reduce facility footprints.

pmc-13059520.title: Binocular versus standard therapy for amblyopia - effect on visual acuity, adherence, and patient or caregiver reported outcomes: protocol for a systematic review
pmc-13059520.creator: Ghada Aleinati, Maryam Alsamhan, Reema AlJassar, Sadan Alhajeri, Alaa AlAli
pmc-13059520.description: BackgroundTraditionally, monocular interventions, like patching, have been the gold standard in amblyopia treatment. However, the current understanding that amblyopia is a binocular rather than monocular condition has inspired a surge in binocular treatments, which encourage the simultaneous use of both eyes.

pmc-13203868.title: The Coronary Venous System in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Narrative Review
pmc-13203868.creator: Ercan Akşit, Cengiz Demir, Uğur Özpınar, Esra Duman Acar
pmc-13203868.description: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a leading cause of death and morbidity worldwide. The pathophysiology of ACS has been largely interpreted through abnormalities of the coronary arteries and the microvascular bed. However, the coronary circulation is fundamentally a closed-loop system, in which the venous component represents the final link in myocardial blood return.

pmc-13302341.creator: E Kandic, I Zdravkovski, F Janushevski, D Cvetkovski, L Poposka, J Taleski
pmc-13302341.description: IntroductionSubclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF) defined by atrial high rate episodes (AHRE) in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) can determine the clinical AF and the stroke risk. Remote monitoring (RM) enables continuous atrial surveillance from the implantation, potentially detecting SCAF earlier than standard care.

pmc-13440276.title: The role of an ultrasound-responsive injectable piezoelectric hydrogel in promoting nerve regeneration and alleviating neuropathic pain
pmc-13440276.creator: Zhaoyang Guo, Weiqian Jiang, Wentao Zhang, Zhongju Liu, Hang Zhou, Hang Liu, Lin Wang, Jiahao Zhang, Xinliang Peng, Xingyu Yang, Maohui Li, Hanchao Liang, Zhongyuan He, Rui Deng, Yongjun Dang, Wei Fu, Keyu Wei, Chao Xie, Zhong-Liang Deng, Youliang Ren, Lei Chu
pmc-13440276.description: BackgroundNeuropathic pain (NP) resulting from peripheral nerve injury (PNI) represents a major clinical challenge. Although electrical stimulation (ES) has demonstrated therapeutic benefits, its clinical translation is limited by the invasiveness of electrode implantation, which often requires large surgical incisions and percutaneous wiring, increasing tissue damage and infection risk.
